title: Trend over time → line / area
use_when: Continuous measure over time; rate of change matters; 1–6 series.
avoid_when: Fewer than 4 points (use a stat + delta), more than ~6 series (small multiples), discrete categories (bars), cumulative composition (stacked area only if parts sum meaningfully).
guidance: Line per series with distinct style (colour + dash/marker), direct end labels instead of a legend where possible, y-axis from zero unless the domain justifies otherwise (say so), consistent time bucketing, downsample >1–2k points, hover/focus reveals values with a crosshair, area fill only for a single series or true cumulative data.

title: Compare categories → bar
avoid_when: >15 categories (table or search), time on the x-axis (line), parts of a whole (stacked bar or waffle).
guidance: Horizontal bars for long labels, sorted by value unless order is meaningful, single colour (highlight one bar for emphasis), zero-based axis always, value labels at bar ends when space allows, grouped bars ≤3 groups, no 3D, no rounded bar ends that misstate length.

title: Part-to-whole → stacked bar, waffle, or (rarely) donut
use_when: Shares of a total with ≤5 parts; one moment in time.
avoid_when: More than 5 slices, comparing parts across many totals (use 100% stacked bars), when precise comparison matters (angles are hard to read).
guidance: Prefer a single stacked horizontal bar or a waffle; a donut only with ≤4 parts, labels with percentages on or beside slices, the largest starting at 12 o'clock, colour-blind-safe palette, and never a 3D pie or exploded slices.

title: Distribution → histogram, box plot, violin, strip
use_when: Shape, spread, outliers of a numeric variable.
avoid_when: Small n (<20, show the points), when the audience needs the raw values (table).
guidance: Histogram with justified bin width (state it), box plot with outliers shown and n labelled, violin only for expert audiences, overlay strips for small n; annotate median/mean explicitly.

title: Relationship → scatter / bubble
use_when: Two numeric variables per item; correlation, clusters, outliers.
avoid_when: Categorical x, >3 encoded dimensions, or thousands of points without density handling.
guidance: Both axes labelled with units, aspect ratio near 1:1 for correlation reading, bubble area (not radius) encodes size with a size legend, opacity for overplotting, trend line only with the method stated, keyboard-accessible point list or table alternative.

title: Two categorical axes × value → heatmap / matrix
use_when: Patterns across day×hour, region×product, correlation matrices.
avoid_when: When exact values are needed (table with conditional formatting is better), rainbow palettes, more than ~50×50 cells without zoom.
guidance: Sequential or diverging perceptual palette (viridis/cividis-style, or a two-hue diverging with a neutral midpoint at a meaningful value), cell values on hover/focus and optionally printed when cells are large, sorted rows/columns to reveal structure, colour scale legend with units.

title: Sequential drop-off → funnel or step bars
use_when: Conversion stages with monotonically decreasing counts.
avoid_when: Stages that are not strictly sequential (use a Sankey or a bar chart), when the funnel shape would distort areas.
guidance: Horizontal bars per stage sorted by sequence with absolute counts and stage-to-stage conversion %, not a trapezoid whose area misleads; highlight the biggest drop; keep colours neutral with one emphasis.

title: Flows between states → Sankey / alluvial
use_when: Quantities moving between categories (budget allocation, user paths, energy).
avoid_when: Few nodes (a table is clearer), audiences unfamiliar with the form, mobile widths.
guidance: ≤~12 nodes, link width proportional to flow, node labels with totals, hover/focus isolates a path, consistent node ordering to reduce crossings, table alternative mandatory.

title: Progress to target → bullet / progress bar, not gauge
use_when: Actual vs target with context bands (poor/ok/good).
avoid_when: Circular gauges waste space and hide comparison; use only for a single real-time reading where the metaphor is native (speed, load).
guidance: Bullet graph: measure bar, target tick, qualitative bands in greys; label the value and target numerically; multiple bullets align for comparison; progress bars must show the numeric value and the whole.

title: Many series or groups → small multiples
use_when: More than ~6 series, or comparing the same chart across regions/products/devices.
avoid_when: When one combined chart with ≤4 series is readable.
guidance: Identical axes across panels (state if not), consistent ordering, panel titles as data labels, shared legend/colour meaning, grid sized so each panel keeps a readable aspect; lazy-render offscreen panels.

title: Geographic values → choropleth or symbol map
use_when: Values keyed by region where geography explains the pattern.
avoid_when: Values that correlate with area/population (normalise per capita or use a bar chart), when regions are too small to see, or when a ranked bar chart answers the question better.
guidance: Choropleth for rates with a sequential palette and ≤7 classes; symbol map for counts with area-scaled circles; equal-area projection; hover/focus tooltip with region name and value; always provide a ranked table alternative; load map data lazily.

title: Uncertainty and forecasts → bands and fans
use_when: Forecasts, confidence intervals, sensor error, A/B results.
avoid_when: Never draw a forecast as a solid continuation of the actual line without marking where the data ends.
guidance: Shaded band(s) with stated interval (e.g. 80%/95%), a vertical 'today' marker, dashed line for point forecast, band opacity that keeps the actual line readable, and text stating the method and interval.

title: Real-time streams → rolling window charts
use_when: Monitoring dashboards, telemetry, trading, wall displays.
avoid_when: Never animate every tick with transitions; never let the axis rescale continuously (readers lose reference).
guidance: Fixed time window that scrolls, stable y-range with occasional stepwise rescale, no per-point animation, thresholds drawn as lines with labels, alert states via colour + icon + text, pause on hover/focus, render on canvas/WebGL beyond a few thousand points, and a 'last updated' timestamp. Wall/TV displays: larger type, fewer panels, high contrast.

title: Chart colour: categorical ≤8, colour-blind safe, plus shape/label
use_when: Any chart with more than one series or category.
avoid_when: Never red/green as the only distinction; never a rainbow for ordered data.
guidance: One categorical palette for the product (Okabe-Ito or Tableau-10-like, ≤8), sequential for ordered, diverging with a neutral midpoint for signed; series also distinguished by line style/marker/direct label; verify with a deuteranopia simulation; dark theme variant of the palette.
